sections.title: What this batch covers
sections.body:
(Beginner to advanced) (5 concepts)

In Batch 1, we learned how to design secure LLM applications.

Now we'll study one of the most important LLM security areas: **Prompt Attacks**.

Prompt attacks target the way an LLM interprets instructions and processes information.

They are especially important in:

- Chatbots
- RAG applications
- Agentic AI systems
- Multi-agent systems
- AI assistants connected to external APIs
- Enterprise copilots

sections.title: 2. Understand the differences
sections.body:
This comparison is particularly important for interviews.

| Scenario | Attack |
|--------|--------|
| User says ignore previous instructions | Direct Prompt Injection |
| PDF contains hidden malicious instructions | Indirect Prompt Injection |
| User tries to bypass model safety restrictions | Jailbreaking |
| LLM reveals its hidden system instructions | Prompt Leakage |
| User attempts to change the assistant's role or policies | System Prompt Manipulation |

One attack can belong to multiple categories.

sections.title: 3. Practical assignment — Enterprise RAG + Agent
sections.body:
Imagine you are developing an enterprise AI assistant with:

- FastAPI
- LangChain
- LangGraph
- OpenAI
- ChromaDB
- PostgreSQL
- Email-sending tools

Answer these scenarios:

1. A user sends malicious instructions directly to your chatbot. Identify the attack and explain how you would detect and mitigate it.

2. A malicious instruction is hidden inside a PDF stored in ChromaDB. Explain the attack and design a secure ingestion and retrieval pipeline.

3. An attacker manipulates the chatbot into bypassing its safety restrictions. How would you evaluate and improve jailbreak resistance?

4. Your chatbot reveals its hidden system instructions. How would you investigate the root cause and prevent sensitive information exposure?

5. Your AI agent sends an email containing confidential information because of malicious instructions in a retrieved document. Design a complete security solution.

steps.label: Rerank
steps.narration: A cross-encoder or LLM reranker reorders candidates for higher precision context.
